verses.1: The LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go to serve me.'
verses.2: If you refuse to let them go, behold, I will strike all your borders with frogs.
verses.3: The river will breed frogs, and they will come up and enter your house, into your bedroom, onto your bed, into the house of your servants, onto your people, into your ovens, and into your kneading bowls.
verses.4: They will come into you and into all your servants, and into every one of your houses."
verses.5: The LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up frogs on the land of Egypt.'"
verses.6: Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.7: The Egyptian magicians did the same by their spells. They brought up frogs on the land of Egypt.
verses.8: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Entreat the LORD to remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD."
verses.9: Moses said to Pharaoh, "When will I entreat for you, for your servants, and for your people, to remove the frogs from you and your houses, leaving them only in the river?"
verses.10: Pharaoh said, "Tomorrow." Moses replied, "May it be as you say, so that you may know that there is none like the LORD our God."
verses.11: The frogs will leave from you, your houses, your servants, and your people. They will remain only in the river."
verses.12: Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs, as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.13: The LORD did as Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, courtyards, and fields.
verses.14: They gathered them together, heap by heap, and the land stank.
verses.15: When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, his heart became heavy, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.
verses.16: The LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground, and let it become lice throughout the land of Egypt.'"
verses.17: Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the ground, and it became lice on the people and on the livestock. Every dust of the ground became lice throughout the land of Egypt.
verses.18: The Egyptian magicians tried to do the same with their spells to drive out the lice, but they could not. The lice remained on the people and the livestock.
verses.19: The magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." But Pharaoh's heart became hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.
verses.20: The LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, for behold, he is going out to the river. Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go to serve me in the wilderness.
verses.21: If you refuse to let them go, behold, I will send swarms of flies on you and your servants and your people and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with swarms of flies, as well as the ground they are on.'
verses.22: I will distinguish that day between the land of Goshen, where my people are, so that there will be no swarms of flies there, so that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land.
verses.23: I will place a boundary between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will happen."
verses.24: The LORD did as he said. A severe plague of flies came into Pharaoh's house and into the houses of his servants, and the entire land of Egypt was ruined by the swarm.
verses.25: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God in the land."
verses.26: Moses said, "It is not proper to do this. For the sacrifices that the Egyptians hate, we would offer to the LORD our God. If we offer the sacrifices that the Egyptians hate in their sight, they will stone us."
verses.27: We will go three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he tells us."
verses.28: Pharaoh said, "I will let you go. You may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness, but do not go far away. Entreat for me."

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: "Let my people go" is a direct translation of "שַׁלַּח אֶת־עַמִּי" (shalach et-‘ammi), a recurring refrain in the dialogue.  
- v. 19: "The finger of God" (δάκτυλος θεοῦ in Greek) is a rare and vivid expression. The Hebrew says "עֶבֶר אֱלֹהִים" (‘ever elohim), literally "the border of God" or "the arm of God," but the Septuagint's "finger" has been adopted due to its clarity and symbolic weight in context.  
- v. 22: "Distinguish" (παραδοξάσω in Greek) reflects the Hebrew "שַׂמְתִּי פְדֻת" (sateti pedut), which conveys a clear separation, not metaphorical "wonder."  
- v. 28: "Do not go far away" (οὐ μακρὰν ἀποτενεῖτε in Greek) is a direct rendering of "לֹא תַרְחִיקוּ" (lo tar’kiku), avoiding archaic phrasing.

[1] The LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go to serve me.'  

[2] If you refuse to let them go, behold, I will strike all your borders with frogs.  

[3] The river will breed frogs, and they will come up and enter your house, into your bedroom, onto your bed, into the house of your servants, onto your people, into your ovens, and into your kneading bowls.  

[4] They will come into you and into all your servants, and into every one of your houses."  

[5] The LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up frogs on the land of Egypt.'"  

[6] Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.  

[7] The Egyptian magicians did the same by their spells. They brought up frogs on the land of Egypt.  

[8] Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Entreat the LORD to remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD."  

[9] Moses said to Pharaoh, "When will I entreat for you, for your servants, and for your people, to remove the frogs from you and your houses, leaving them only in the river?"  

[10] Pharaoh said, "Tomorrow." Moses replied, "May it be as you say, so that you may know that there is none like the LORD our God."  

[11] The frogs will leave from you, your houses, your servants, and your people. They will remain only in the river."  

[12] Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs, as Pharaoh had commanded.  

[13] The LORD did as Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, courtyards, and fields.  

[14] They gathered them together, heap by heap, and the land stank.  

[15] When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, his heart became heavy, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.  

[16] The LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground, and let it become lice throughout the land of Egypt.'"  

[17] Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the ground, and it became lice on the people and on the livestock. Every dust of the ground became lice throughout the land of Egypt.  

[18] The Egyptian magicians tried to do the same with their spells to drive out the lice, but they could not. The lice remained on the people and the livestock.  

[19] The magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." But Pharaoh's heart became hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.  

[20] The LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, for behold, he is going out to the river. Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go to serve me in the wilderness.  

[21] If you refuse to let them go, behold, I will send swarms of flies on you and your servants and your people and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with swarms of flies, as well as the ground they are on.'  

[22] I will distinguish that day between the land of Goshen, where my people are, so that there will be no swarms of flies there, so that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land.  

[23] I will place a boundary between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will happen."  

[24] The LORD did as he said. A severe plague of flies came into Pharaoh's house and into the houses of his servants, and the entire land of Egypt was ruined by the swarm.  

[25] Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God in the land."  

[26] Moses said, "It is not proper to do this. For the sacrifices that the Egyptians hate, we would offer to the LORD our God. If we offer the sacrifices that the Egyptians hate in their sight, they will stone us."  

[27] We will go three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he tells us."  

[28] Pharaoh said, "I will let you go. You may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness, but do not go far away. Entreat for me."
